question: An HR team uses Claude to generate a shortlist recommendation from a stack of job applications. Before any candidate is rejected based on this shortlist, what should the team do?
options: A) Have a recruiter review the underlying applications to check for bias or overlooked qualified candidates
B) Shorten the job description so future applicant pools are easier for the model to rank consistently
C) Reject every applicant left off the shortlist since the model already considered all submitted application details
D) Ask Claude to regenerate the shortlist a second time and merge both lists into the final decision
correct_answers: A) Have a recruiter review the underlying applications to check for bias or overlooked qualified candidates
explanations: Correct. Employment decisions carry legal and fairness risk, so a recruiter should review the underlying applications to catch bias or qualified candidates the model may have overlooked.
Incorrect. Changing the job description does not address whether the current shortlist decision requires human review before candidates are rejected.
Incorrect. Rejecting candidates purely based on an unreviewed AI shortlist risks embedding bias or errors into a consequential employment decision.
Incorrect. Merging two outputs from the same model does not introduce the independent human judgment needed to catch bias in a hiring decision.
